punchline: Brené Brown says if you are brave often enough you will fall, and she calls that the physics of vulnerability.
thirty_sec: In 1910 Theodore Roosevelt praised the man in the arena, face marked with dust and sweat and blood, who errs and comes up short again and again. Brené Brown picked up the picture and asked what happens after he falls. Her first law: if you're brave often enough, you will fall. She only takes feedback from people who are in the arena too.
